title: Hot/Cold Cache Hierarchy — Architecture Review & Sprint Retro
summary: Notes from architecture review covering a two-tier hot/cold KV cache model for inference runtime. Decision to adopt a hybrid GPU-hot / CPU-warm / local NVMe-cold tier with consistent-hash sharding and async prefetching. Action items and rollout plan included.
content:
Meeting: Hot/Cold Cache Hierarchy — Architecture Review & Sprint Retro
Date: 2025-02-12 10:00-11:30 PT
Location: Zoom + #serving-runtime // recording linked in Confluence
Attendees: Asha Patel (owner, notes), Miguel Ortiz, Liang Wu, Priya Menon, Ethan Gomez, Riley Chen, + SRE on-call (TBD)
Objectives:
- Review design proposals for multi-tier KV cache (GPU hot, CPU warm, NVMe cold) to reduce per-token cost and tail latency
- Validate eviction/pinning strategies and multi-tenant fairness model
- Agree on rollout experiment plan and metrics to measure

Context / Why now:
- Growing variance in sequence lengths and session locality leads to inefficient GPU memory utilization. Current single-layer hot KV (GPU-only) causes either high tail-latency when misses cascade to cold store, or excessive model offloads when we over-provision hotset.
- We have a small spike that showed 12–18% cost savings if we can avoid NVMe misses for ~60% of conversational replays. Need a production-ready design that is safe for multi-tenant clusters and private deployments.

Proposal overview (recap):
- Three logical tiers: GPU-hot (per-GPU KV shard), CPU-warm (node-local DRAM LRU), NVMe-cold (local SSD or remote object store).
- Sharding: consistent-hash across GPUs for the hot tier, with per-tenant hotset reservations (soft and hard limits). CPU-warm is fed by async evictions from GPU-hot and by a lightweight admission policy for new keys.
- Eviction: segmented LRU in GPU-hot (hot vs long-lived pinned keys) + time-decay scoring for CPU-warm to prefer conversational locality.
- Miss handling: synchronous fallback path to CPU-warm, async prefetch to GPU-hot after one successful CPU-warm hit, and background population for top-N keys based on recent access frequency.

Design alternatives considered (short):
1) Centralized hot directory service that tracks hot keys per cluster (rejected): adds single point of contention and strong coupling with control plane; increases metadata traffic.
2) Purely dynamic hotset computed via global telemetry (rejected for v1): telemetry lag and complexity; keep for v2 experimentation.
3) Per-tenant strict pinning (opt-in) vs soft reservations (chosen soft): strict pinning provides isolation but may hurt bin-packing and utilization. Soft reservations with eviction priority chosen to balance isolation and efficiency.

Benchmarks / experimental numbers (spike, internal):
- Workload: multi-tenant chat benchmark (mix of short Q&A and long back-and-forth), 60k qps synthetic, 95th-token latency baseline (GPU-only) = 320ms.
- CPU-warm prototype (8GB per node) reduced end-to-end 95p token latency to 210ms on test harness for mixed traffic when hotset fit was ~35% larger than GPU-hot capacity.
- Observed CPU-warm hit rate: 28% (of misses from GPU-hot). After enabling async prefetch to GPU-hot for top-100 keys, tail latency dropped further ~7%.
- Cost estimate: projected 9–14% per-token infrastructure cost reduction for customer profiles with >40% repeated-key locality.

Key architecture decisions (agreed):
- Adopt hybrid tier model (GPU-hot / CPU-warm / NVMe-cold) for v1 rollout.
- Sharding: consistent hash ring per model family; add virtual replicas per GPU to improve distribution.
- Eviction policy: segmented LRU on GPU-hot (separate small pinned segment + LRU moving window), CPU-warm uses time-decayed LFU-esque scoring derived from recency+frequency; NVMe-cold remains object store with TTL and cheap garbage collection.
- Admission policy: rate-limited admission into GPU-hot; heuristics to promote CPU-warm hits into GPU-hot (threshold=3 hits within window=5m).
- Safety: implement a circuit-breaker that prevents GPU prefetch storms (max concurrent prefetches per GPU=64) and a global admission throttle triggered by GPU mem pressure > 85%.

Rollout & experiments plan:
Phase 0 — Canary (2 weeks):
- Deploy CPU-warm on 10% of nodes behind a feature flag. Route 1% of production traffic (shadow reads) to collect hit rates and latency traces. Owners: Priya (deploy), Ethan (telemetry).
- Success criteria: CPU-warm hit rate >= 20% on canary tenants and no increase in 99p latency on control pods.

Phase 1 — Limited opt-in (4 weeks):
- Enable async prefetch promotion for a small cohort of tenants. Tenant teams can opt-in to soft reservations. Owners: Asha (coord), Miguel (runtime), Riley (ops).
- Measure tail-latency, prefetch cost vs benefit, and GPU memory churn.

Phase 2 — Gradual rollout (8–12 weeks):
- Ramp to 50% nodes and add dynamic heuristics for top-key detection. Add telemetry dashboards and rollback playbooks.

Operational concerns & mitigations:
- Telemetry volume: push sampled traces for prefetch events and maintain aggregate counters (per-model, per-tenant) to avoid metadata hot spots.
- Multi-tenant fairness: use tenant QoS credits and per-tenant admission windows; do not allow a single tenant to evict pinned keys beyond their reservation without admin override.
- Consistency: eventual consistency acceptable for KV entries (keys are model activations), but we must ensure correctness for conversational KV that is used across replicas — decided to replicate pinned keys synchronously for small pinned sets.
- Recovery: on node restart, rebuild GPU-hot from CPU-warm using top-N prefetch + background warm-up.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Memory accounting model across heterogeneous GPU types (A100 vs H100 equivalents). Action: Liang to propose an abstraction for hotset sizing (memory-efficiency score) by 2025-02-19.
- How to measure/price prefetch overhead in tenant billing models (cost visibility in Console). Action: Miguel + Finance touchpoint (FIN-?) to propose metering approach.
- Eviction fairness for bursty tenants: need a simulation to verify edge cases where many short-lived keys evict long-lived conversational pins. Action: Riley to run simulator and report by 2025-02-28.

Risks called out:
- Prefetch storms causing transient OOMs: mitigated via prefetch concurrency caps and admission throttles.
- Telemetry lag causing stale promotion decisions: mitigate with short-window counters and exponential decay.
- NVMe cold-store write amplification under heavy churn: plan to cap cold-store write rate and prioritize dedup semantics in v1.

Action items (owner + due):
- Priya: land CPU-warm feature-flagged deploy + helm chart changes (due 2025-02-18).
- Ethan: dashboard for CPU-warm/GPU-hot hit rates + prefetch telemetry sampling config (due 2025-02-17).
- Liang: memory-efficiency abstraction proposal and sample calculations across GPU SKUs (due 2025-02-19).
- Miguel: draft billing/metering proposal for prefetch cost attribution (touch finance) (due 2025-02-21).
- Riley: build simulator for eviction fairness edge cases and run 3 scenarios (due 2025-02-28).
- Asha: prepare canary run playbook and rollback steps; coordinate on-call for canary window (due 2025-02-16).

Follow-ups / next meetings:
- Short sync 2025-02-18 to confirm canary readiness and finalize telemetry thresholds.
- Architecture retro to review canary results (target week of 2025-03-03).

Notes / miscellaneous:
- Team agreed to keep central directory idea as an experimental research track (INF-8337) but not to block v1 on it.
- Suggested small change to promo heuristics: include namespace-scoped recency to avoid global hot keys from drowning out tenant-local conversational keys.

Adjourned: 11:28 PT
Recorded by: Asha Patel
